confirmed.description: Nagoji is wearing a rust-red sash wrapped around his waist over the cream shirt. This is the red sash from the commander sheet leaking into his chapter 6 look. The bible's chapter 6 row says village cotton dhoti and simple cream shirt only, the script says he wears no sash, and none of his other chapter 6 panels show one. Readers may take it as a costume change or a return to rank.
confirmed.evidence: Seated meditating figure with eyes closed. A bright rust-red cloth band crosses his waist below the shirt hem, at roughly x 300-420, y 760-790 in the 1838x2775 render. Nagoji's waist shows no red sash in 5.2, 6.1, 7.4, 8.3, 10.1, 11.5 or 12.1.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 7, panel 7.1 (render page-07.png, 1838x2775). I cropped the panel at about x 150-920, y 360-930. Nagoji sits cross-legged with his eyes closed. A broad rust-red cloth band is wrapped around his waist over the cream shirt, just below its hem, at roughly x 300-420, y 760-790. It is a saturated, clearly drawn sash, not shading or a dhoti border, and it stays easy to see at print size.

Neither the bible nor the script allows it. The bible's chapter 6 row for Nagoji says only "Village cotton dhoti and simple cream shirt, bare-headed, hair loose or tied back, hands still bandaged". The red sash belongs to the commander sheet (chapters 7 onward) and to pre-capture memory panels only. Script 1.2 says "no sword, no sash, no turban", and 12.4 and 12.5 repeat NO sash.

The panel also breaks continuity with the panels next to it. In 7.2 and 7.4 (same scene, same mat, same reverse angle) his waist shows only the cream shirt and dhoti with no red. Thumbnails of pages 5, 6, 8 and 12 show no sash on him anywhere else in the chapter.

The sash is the same red as the background Travancore guards' waist cloths, so a reader could take it as a costume change or an early return to his commander rank. His identity is correct (face, hair, ear stud, bandaged hands), so this is a localized costume error. Severity is major, not blocker: 7.1 needs its waist redrawn without the sash.

confirmed.description: Ibrahim's LEFT ear-to-jaw scar cannot be seen. The panel's whole staging exists so that sea light falls on this scar (the adaptation notes put the open side on the king's right for this reason). His left cheek and jaw are either covered by a balloon tail or the scar was not drawn.
confirmed.evidence: Ibrahim's face sits at roughly x 470-560, y 400-470. The 'Beyond that, trust is for priests.' balloon tail comes in from screen right and sits on his left cheek and jaw, and the visible part of his face shows no scar line. Compare 1.2 and 2.3, where the scar does show.

verdict.reason:
The finding is accurate, but it is minor, not major. On page 9, panel 9.1, Ibrahim is in three-quarter view facing the platform, so his left cheek is on screen right. The tip of the 'Beyond that, trust is for priests.' balloon tail comes in from screen right and stops on that cheek at about x 510, y 450 (full-resolution pixels). It covers his left ear and the back of the cheek, which is where the ear-to-jaw scar should start. In the parts of that cheek and the jaw-line beard that are still visible, there is no scar line. By contrast, the scar is a clear red line through the beard in 2.3 and is also visible in 1.2. So the scar is not visible in 9.1, and the script's note about sea light catching it is not met.

Why it is minor: Ibrahim's face is only about 50 to 60 px wide at 300 DPI, roughly 4 to 5 mm in print. At that size the scar would be a hairline even if fully drawn. He is shown at a similar size in 1.4, and no scar shows there either. The white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, pale vest with bulging pockets and striped shoulder cloth make him unmistakable, so his identity is not in doubt. No caption or dialogue in this panel mentions the scar, so no story beat is lost. The fix is cheap and also good lettering practice: move the tail tip off his cheek toward his mouth or the open air beside his head, so the left ear and jaw are clear.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute this. A zoomed crop of page 7, panel 1 (/Users/roshanvenugopal/Documents/github/nagoji/output/comic-v15-full-redo/chapters/ch06-split/renders/r7/page-07.png) shows present-day Nagoji with a broad rust-red cloth sash wrapped and knotted at his waist over the cream shirt. He is seated on the mat with bandaged hands, so this is not a memory panel. Only the background (ships, burning quay, horse) is the memory image, and the script's 7.1 does not dress him in his old Maratha clothes. The sash is a solid colour band across the middle of a top-tier panel, so it will show clearly in print.

Nothing in the source files allows it:
- CONTINUITY.md, Nagoji's chapter 6 row: "Village cotton dhoti and simple cream shirt, bare-headed, hair loose or tied back, hands still bandaged." No sash.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming this one. In the zoomed crop of page 11, panel 5 (right third), Varma sits in a tall, dark, carved armchair with a red cushion. A red-carpeted stair with gold edging runs up to it. Ramayyan sits in a matching red-cushioned carved chair beside him, holding his palm-leaf bundle, and there is no low table. The script for 11.5 says only "on the platform above him", and the fixed hall plan (script line 43 and the notes at 374) puts the king on a slightly raised wooden platform, with Ramayyan's low table at his left hand. Varma sits cross-legged on a mat on the low wooden platform in 2.2, 4.1, 8.1, 10.5 and 12.2, and Ramayyan sits at his low table or on the platform beside him in 2.4, 4.1 and 8.1. confirmed.description: The hall set changes between pages. Page 2 (and pages 7, 8, 10 and 12) establish a dark wooden pavilion: carved wooden pillars, mat floor, a low wooden platform, and the map lying on the mat. Pages 3 to 5 instead show a different room: white or grey plastered walls, stone columns, a polished marble floor, a red-carpeted stair up to a dais, and Varma seated behind a raised map table. The script fixes one hall for the whole chapter. Props drift as well: the map is on the mat in 2.2, on a table in 3.1, gone in 4.1 (his spear is gone too), and on a table again in 6.3 and 7.3.
confirmed.evidence: 3.1: white back wall, red carpet runner and steps, marble floor, map on a low table. 3.3: grey stone pillars and grey wall. 4.1 and 4.2: grey plaster wall and stone floor. 5.2: stone columns and tiled marble floor. Compare 2.1, 2.5, 8.1 and 8.4: carved dark wood pillars and mat floors.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming this as major. I checked a zoomed crop of page 3, panel 1 against pages 2, 6, 7 and 8. The script fixes one hall plan for every hall panel (page 2 intro and the "Hall plan" note). Page 2.1 shows that hall as carved dark-wood pillars, dark rafters and mat floors, with the sea through the open side on the left, and 2.2 has Varma on a low wooden platform with the map on the mat. Page 3.1 shows a different room: a bare cream plaster back wall, plain columns, a polished stone or marble floor, a red-carpeted flight of steps up to a dais, the map on a raised table, and Ramayyan standing instead of sitting at his low table. Through the open side on the left there is a hilltop fort and palms, not the sea. The rest of pages 3 to 5 stays in that second room. 3.3 has grey stone columns, a grey wall and a hill fort where the sea should be. 4.1 and 4.2 show a grey plaster wall over a polished stone floor. 5.1 has plaster, an arcade and marble, and 5.2 has stone pillars, a tiled floor and a hill fort instead of the sea. By page 8 the art is back in the carved-wood hall with mats and the sea. At print size a reader would think the audience had moved rooms, against a script that fixes one hall. The prop sub-claims are weaker. The script asks for the map on the mat only in 2.2, and does not require a map or spear in 4.1. So the missing map and spear in 4.1, and the table in 7.3, are slight drift rather than errors. This is not a blocker: identity, lettering and story beats are all intact. The fault is a localized set and background error across pages 3 to 5, and fixing it means redrawing those backgrounds.

confirmed.description: Varma and Ramayyan both sit in carved, high-backed, red-upholstered throne chairs. verdict.reason: The finding is confirmed. I zoomed into page 11, panel 11.5 (bottom-right of the full-width panel). Varma sits upright in a dark carved armchair with a high back and red upholstery. Ramayyan sits next to him at screen right in a second chair with armrests, a red cushion and a gilt finial, in front of the conch banner. Both are on a stepped dais with a red carpet. There is no floor mat and no low table. The chairs are easy to see at print size, so this is not too slight to matter. Nothing in the script or bible allows it. The fixed HALL PLAN in the script (page 2 intro and the end notes) gives Ramayyan a low table, and 2.2 puts the map "on the mat before him" for Varma. Every other hall panel draws exactly that. The rating is major, not blocker: identities, costumes, the beat and the lettering are all correct, and the error is limited to the seating and dais in one panel, so redrawing that panel fixes it.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's off-panel line ('And their infantry...') is meant to sit with the inset. Instead its balloon sits over the inset's right border, and its long tail runs down through the map to the panel's bottom border beside Varma's pointing finger. Ramayyan's balloon covers the bottom of the inset. Together they half-bury the stylus inset, and the tail makes the speaker unclear.
confirmed.evidence: The Nagoji balloon spans about x 395-940, y 2075-2245, which overlaps the inset (about x 160-555, y 2055-2250). Its tail tip is at about (688,2530) on the bottom border, next to Varma's finger at about (900,2490). Ramayyan's balloon (x 150-650, y 2250-2490) covers the inset's lower edge.

verdict.reason:
The overlap is real but the harm is smaller than claimed, so I am downgrading this from major to minor. I checked page 6, panel 6.3 at full resolution, with zooms on the inset and on the tail tip.

What the art shows:
- **Nagoji's balloon** covers about the right third of the inset (roughly x 390-555), over the end of the writing board and the cloth.
- **Nagoji's tail** is a straight line about 300 px long (about 1 inch at print size). It runs between Ramayyan's balloon and Varma's arm and stops on a small island on the map, about 7 px above the bottom border. It does not quite cross the border.
- **Varma's finger** is about 230 px to the right of the tail tip (about (915, 2480)).

Why the claimed harm is overstated:
1. **The inset is not half-buried.** The key action is fully visible: Ramayyan's hand, the stylus and its tip touching the board.
2. **Ramayyan's balloon does not cover the inset.** Its top edge sits just below the inset's bottom border. Its tail reaches up into the inset to the stylus tip, which is the correct way to tag the speaker, since the inset shows Ramayyan's hand.
3. **The speaker is not really unclear.** The tail points at no visible character, and Varma has his own "[in Malayalam]" balloon. The line also continues Nagoji's speech from 6.1 and 6.2. Pointing down toward the bottom border reads as the usual signal for an off-panel speaker.
4. **The script allows this placement.** It only asks that the line sit with the inset, and a balloon overlapping an inset border is normal practice.

What is left is a polish fix:
- The tail is long, runs through the art, and stops on the map instead of crossing the border.
- The balloon covers part of the inset's right side.
- Fix: move Nagoji's balloon closer to the inset, and shorten the tail so it crosses the bottom border directly.

confirmed.description: The page grid is ragged. Each of the five rows is inset to a different width, and none fills the live area. The page has a stepped, pyramid outline unlike the approved Chapter 1 pages, which keep a full-width grid with at most one inset row.

confirmed.description: Below a full-width 8.1, each of the next three rows is inset to a different width, so the page's left and right edges zig-zag. This does not match the Chapter 1 standard.

verdict.reason:

The next three rows are each centred but inset by a different amount: 8.2 spans 241-1596 (93 px, about 7.9 mm each side), 8.3 spans 217-1619 (69 px, about 5.8 mm) and 8.4 spans 265-1571 (117 px, about 9.9 mm). The same pattern appears on Chapter 6 pages 2, 10 (the worst, with insets up to 341 px) and 11, so the cause is the Chapter 6 layout fit, not this page alone.

confirmed.description: Ibrahim's first balloon ('As far as one can trust a man who owes you his life and hates the same enemies.') is squeezed into a narrow column of 10 lines with one to three words each. verdict.reason: I confirmed the problem but rate it minor, not major. In the original render (1838x2775), page 9, panel 9.1 has Ibrahim's first balloon ("As far as one can trust a man who owes you his life and hates the same enemies.") set as a tall, narrow pill of 10 lines with 1 to 3 words each. It bleeds off the panel's left, top and bottom borders, and its right edge nearly touches his raised left hand. That breaks the sentence into a choppy read and looks cramped next to the wide two-line balloon beside it. It is not a blocker or a major issue. It is still clearly a speech balloon; bleeding a balloon off the panel edge is a normal comics technique. The fix is polish: reflow the text into a wider, shorter balloon of about 4 to 5 lines in the upper left so it clears the borders.

confirmed.description: Ramayyan's second balloon ('He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat...') is a tall column of 9 lines with two or three words each. It runs to the right border and the bottom of the panel and covers Ramayyan's whole body below the chest.

confirmed.description: The background of this large panel has a visible vertical stitching seam. The carved wall frieze is sharp to the left of the seam and blurred and offset to the right, with hard black edge lines where it breaks.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 4, panel 4.2 (the large bottom panel). I zoomed in on the source PNG (1838x2775) and found a hard vertical compositing seam at about x 1180. confirmed.description: Both of Ibrahim's tails stab into his face: the first ends on his eye and the second on his cheek. The second balloon's body covers his ear, which is where the scar the panel is framed to show begins.
confirmed.evidence: Tail 1's tip is at about (1068,940), on Ibrahim's left eye. Tail 2's tip is at about (1083,970), on his cheek beside the scar. The balloon edge covers his ear and turban at about x 1150-1240.

verdict.reason: The claim holds up after zooming into page 1, panel 1.2 (crop of the area around x 980-1200, y 860-1060). Tail 1, from the "Gifts. confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tails: both of Ibrahim's lines point at Nagoji, so Nagoji appears to name the king and the diwan and to remind himself about gifts.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. I cropped page 2, panel 2.3 at full resolution (source pixels about 922-1688 x 987-1488) and the art shows the problem. The tail of "Marthanda Varma. And his diwan." runs down and to the right and ends in the curls at the back and top of Nagoji's head, above his ear. It stops well short of Ibrahim, whose mouth is further right, behind the beard under the turban. The tail of "Remember what I said about gifts." rises from the lower balloon and ends on Nagoji's neck and shoulder, at his collar. It also stops short of Ibrahim's beard and mouth. Both balloons sit on the left over Nagoji's profile, and nothing points at Ibrahim. At print size a reader takes both lines as Nagoji's. Neither the script nor the bible allows this. verdict.reason: Downgraded from major to minor. This is a lettering fix, not a misattribution. On page 3, panel 3.1 the tail of the second balloon ("He comes from Portuguese chains...") is short and stops at the screen-left edge of Nagoji's shirt-tail. That is at hip height, beside his hand, so the tip does sit on the wrong man. The claim fails on direction. I extended the tail's line upward: it runs past Ibrahim's gesturing hand and lands about 40px in front of his mouth, next to the first balloon's tail. So the tail leans up-left toward Ibrahim, not straight up at Nagoji. Nagoji is bowing with his back to the reader and his head far above the tip, so nothing ties the tail to his mouth. Three other things identify the speaker: the line is in the third person ("He comes..."), it follows Ibrahim's "Your Majesty" balloon, and Ibrahim's open hand presents Nagoji. A reader is unlikely to think Nagoji is introducing himself, and the script gives both lines to Ibrahim, which the page does. verdict.reason: I could not refute this. On page 6, panel 6.2 (r7 render, area around x 1000-1300, y 1250-1650 at full size), both balloon tails are short wedges that end inside the stain. The script gives both lines to NAGOJI, and the cast for this panel is only nagoji and varma, so the padre and musketeer are silent hearsay figures. The tails do angle down-left, and extended they would roughly reach Nagoji's head. But they stop on the padre and the musketeer, and the padre is the panel's centred focal figure, so a reader's first reading is that he speaks the lines. The text works against that reading: a padre saying "their padres" is odd. The tails are large and plain at print size. The balloon layout is fine; only the two tails are wrong and need to be extended down to Nagoji. So this is a localized major problem (wrong speaker tail), not a blocker.

The panel opens with a separate "[in Malayalam]" balloon tailed to Varma, as the script's chapter convention requires (script line 73, with the 8.4 tag at lines 221-223). Panel 8.2 already sets up Ramayyan as the voice saying "He says...". The tail is also angled toward Ramayyan, and the next balloon in the same panel is tailed clearly to him. verdict.reason:

Page 7, panel 7.1 (/Users/roshanvenugopal/Documents/github/nagoji/output/comic-v15-full-redo/chapters/ch06-split/renders/r7/page-07.png) shows Nagoji seated cross-legged with a broad rust-red sash wound around the waist of his cream shirt, just above his bandaged hands. Nothing in the bible or the script allows it:

- The script says "no sash" outright at 1.2, and "NO sash" at 12.4 and 12.5.

That last point matters here, because 7.1 also shows a memory scene behind Nagoji. Putting the commander's red sash on the present-day figure in that panel blurs exactly the distinction the script was protecting.

It also breaks continuity with the panels on either side. In 6.2 and 7.4 the same seated Nagoji wears his shirt loose over the dhoti with no sash. refuted.description: The tail of Ibrahim's second balloon ('He comes from Portuguese chains and storm water...') points up at Nagoji's bowing back, not at Ibrahim. Readers will take it as Nagoji introducing himself in the third person.

Extending its centre line from the base at about (688,952) through the tip passes through Ibrahim's outstretched forearm at about (577,700) and comes within about 35 px of his mouth at about (500,600). (2) The text says "He comes from...", which names Nagoji in the third person. It also follows straight on from Ibrahim's first balloon, whose tail clearly reaches Ibrahim's mouth. (3) Ibrahim's mouth is open and his palm is held out toward Nagoji. Nagoji is bowed, head down, with his back to the reader. Seen at about one third of full size, roughly how the printed page reads, the tail looks like it points into the gap between the two men, leaning toward Ibrahim. refuted.reason: I'm refuting this. I cropped panel 2.3 at full 300 DPI resolution (page crop 920,985 to 1690,1490, and a 2x zoom of 1200,1050 to 1560,1360). The coordinates in the report are about right. Tail 1 ends at about (1367,1135) on the back of Nagoji's head. Tail 2 ends at about (1400,1230) on the hair and collar at the back of his neck. The conclusion that the tails 'end on the listener' does not hold up, for four reasons. (1) Both tails point straight at Ibrahim's mouth and beard, at about (1435,1195). Extend either one and it hits him. Each tip stops only about 32 to 35 px short of Ibrahim's turban or beard, which is under 3 mm at print size, right at the seam between the two heads. (2) Both tips land on the back of Nagoji's head and neck. Nagoji is in strict profile facing screen left, with his mouth at about (1295,1200), on the opposite side of his head from both tips. Readers attribute a tail to the mouth it points at, not to the back of a head. (3) This is the whisper staging the script asks for ('Ibrahim at Nagoji's ear, lips barely moving'). Ibrahim's mouth sits directly behind Nagoji's head, and both balloons are on the left so that Ibrahim's face stays clear and the reading order works. So any tail reaching his mouth has to cross Nagoji, and the letterer's tips are about as close as this layout allows. Nagoji is visibly listening and Ibrahim is visibly leaning in to speak, so the attribution to Ibrahim is clear at print size. (4) The break 'Marthanda Varma. And / his diwan.' is awkward but fully readable. A break at the sentence boundary ('Marthanda Varma. / And his diwan.') would be nicer, but that is optional polish, not a lettering error. Nothing here is a major problem.

The tail points away from Varma's head, not toward it, and readers link a tail to the head it aims at, not to an arm it passes. Varma's own "[in Malayalam]" balloon has a tail running down to his mouth, which is the intended split. The words "He says, perhaps." are third-person translator speech that the king could not be saying about himself. The next balloon, "And he asks Ibrahim...", has its tail clearly on Ramayyan, so the pair reads as his translation. Nothing in the art reads as Varma speaking in Konkani, so the major claim fails. At most this is a polish note: extending the tail about 80 px to touch Ramayyan's shoulder would remove any slight doubt.

minors.description: Panel 5.1 is scripted as 'Small' but fills the top half of the page, which squeezes 5.2, the action beat (Ramayyan points with his stylus as Nagoji sits).
minors.evidence: The Varma close-up runs from y≈260 to 1055 in the 2000 px display, about half the page. 5.2 takes the rest.

minors.description: The planned scar beat is lost. The script builds the hall plan so that sea light 'catches the scar along his LEFT jaw', but no scar reads. The shot is also a small full-figure long shot, not the scripted medium.
minors.evidence: Zoomed, Ibrahim's face shows no scar. The tail of 'Beyond that, trust is for priests.' lands on his left cheek and jaw, where the scar should be. He is drawn head to sandals, small in the frame.

minors.description: The scripted 'low angle from floor level ... looking up past [the platform's] edge' is drawn at roughly eye level. A balloon covers most of Varma, the second figure the script asks for.
minors.evidence: No platform edge appears in the foreground. The balloon 'Yet your own masters failed to keep you from their dungeons.' covers Varma's torso and the hand holding the upright spear. Only his face shows above it.

minors.description: An awkward crop: the top border cuts through Nagoji's brow, so the scripted beat 'he does not drop his eyes' sits right on the panel edge.
minors.evidence: Zoomed, the panel's top line crosses just above Nagoji's eyes. The top of his head and his forehead are out of frame, while the lower half of the panel is mostly balloons and lap.

minors.description: Crop: Varma's turban is cut by the top border, so the jewelled peacock-feather crest that the script repeats in every Varma panel is out of frame.
minors.evidence: In the narrow bottom strip, only the lower band of the turban shows above Varma's brow. The feather and jewel are cropped away. The spear taps, the motion ticks and the bird on the parapet are all present.

minors.description: The script asks for 'Dark rafters and open hall space above him for the balloons'. Instead, Nagoji's head touches the top border and a balloon overlaps the back of his head.
minors.evidence: The top of Nagoji's hair is cut by the panel's top line. The right balloon 'I can show your riders...' overlaps his ear and the back of his head. There is no rafter space above him.

minors.description: Panel 11.4 is scripted 'Full width' to plant the Chapter 7 shore clearly, but it is drawn as an inset narrower than the page's other tiers.
minors.evidence: The panel spans x≈220 to 1105, against 108 to 1217 for the full-width tiers 11.1 and 11.5 above and below it.

minors.description: The scripted 'high' shot from the entrance end is drawn at eye level. Varma sits on a carved high-backed chair rather than on the platform mat, which works against 12.2's 'too many lives to sit on that mat'.
minors.evidence: The camera is level with the seated men. Behind Varma is an ornate dark wooden throne-chair back with armrest. In every other hall panel he sits cross-legged on a mat.

minors.description: The hand placement differs from the script, which puts the bandaged hand on the plain knot of the cotton dhoti, below the hem of the cream shirt.
minors.evidence: The hand rests on the shirt fabric at the waist and hip. The shirt hangs well below the hand, and no dhoti knot is visible. The hip is correctly free of any weapon or sash.

minors.description: Nagoji's off-panel line was meant to sit 'in the inset'. Instead, its long tail drops down into the map near Varma's pointing hand, which muddles who speaks.
minors.evidence: 'And their infantry do not know what to do with sudden horse on the flank.' sits beside the inset, and its tail runs down to the bottom border on the map's coastline, just left of Varma's finger.

minors.description: The second line of Nagoji's speech points into the memory scene rather than at the present-day Nagoji.
minors.evidence: The tail of 'Someone who has watched their neat formations falter...' ends in the splash at Kanka's hooves. Present-day Nagoji sits at the lower left, so a reader could take the memory rider as the speaker.

minors.description: Ibrahim's balloon tails stab into his face. One lands in his eye, and the other's tip sits on the cheek where his scripted LEFT-jaw scar should read.
minors.evidence: Zoomed, the tail of 'Gifts. Information costs...' ends at Ibrahim's right eye. The tail of 'When we reach the hall...' ends on his left cheek, just above the faint scar line.
